For the left connection between the amygdala and the OFC, we found a decreasing trend of effective connectivity in pretreatment patients with MDD compared to healthy control (the top‐down connection from OFC_L to Amg_L: t = 1.577, P = 0.1230) (Figure 5 ).
The MNI coordinates of the ROIs centers were as follows: the left amygdala (−24, −1, −18), left OFC (−31, 51, −10), right amygdala (28, 1, −18), and right OFC (34, 53, −11).

value: For the left connection between the amygdala and the OFC, there was a decreasing trend of effective connectivity in pretreatment patients with MDD compared to healthy controls, specifically in the top-down connection from OFC_L to Amg_L.
Compared to healthy controls, causal interactions between the OFC and amygdala were generally lower in patients with MDD, suggesting weaker influences between these two nodes.

There was a significant negative connection from the OFC to the amygdala in the control group, implicating inhibition of amygdala activity by the OFC; this inhibitory regulation was absent in patients with MDD.

Following 8 weeks of antidepressant treatment, the abnormal effective connectivity between the amygdala and OFC in the left hemisphere was normalized, whereas the right-sided connectivity remained abnormal.
